population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: ever 26.0% − current 17.9% = 8.1 pts of adults have used and are off now. About 6.5 pts of current users are on a second or later course, mostly 2028 stoppers who restarted on $39–69 generic semaglutide, and ≈2.6 pts of the off-now group restarted and stopped again. (6.5+2.6)/26.0 = 35% cycled. This is down from 40% because 9.5 pts of new ever-users dilute the share. It fits one-year persistence rising from ~35% to ~50% once cost stopped forcing people off. Current users ≈ 48.0M of ~268M adults, and ever-users ≈ 69.7M. The age-band check uses 2030 adult shares (18–29 19.5%, 30–49 33%, 50–64 22%, 65+ 25.5%): 1.85+6.11+6.16+3.83 ≈ 17.9. The bottom third rose most (6.5→14.2) on generic semaglutide through Medicaid, quitlines and cash. The top third (13.5→21) moved up-market to retatrutide, tirzepatide and monitored 'metabolic' regimens. Off-drug people: ~21.7M who used and stopped, many of them over 65 after DEXA results, plus women stopping for pregnancy and some 'holiday' takers who never restarted; and ~198M who never used, now mostly people outside BMI criteria, the uninsured in non-expansion states who distrust or can't keep up with prescriber visits, and people who decline. Pediatric: ~0.8% of ~73M under-18s (≈590k), mostly adolescents 12+ on generic semaglutide. Children under 12 remain rare. No child has more than ~7 years of exposure.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge expired Dec 2029. CMMI replaced it on Jan 2030 with the Medicare Metabolic Health Demonstration, which is generic-first: Medicare pays ~$55/month for generic semaglutide ($10 copay) and $245 for brand tirzepatide or retatrutide ($50 copay) after step therapy or documented failure. Continued coverage requires ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered, and enrollees 65+ need an annual DEXA and a resistance-training counselling visit. Obesity-indication enrollees ≈4.5M: 2.7M generic × $55 × 12 = $1.78B, plus 1.8M brand × $245 × 12 = $5.29B, ≈ $7.1B/yr. Medicare overall (Part D diabetes plus the demo) pays ~22% of fills ≈ 10.6M users (≈9.9M of ~66M adults 65+ at 15%, plus ~0.7M disabled under-65). Medicaid pays ~14% of fills ≈ 6.7M users, ~85% on generic: 5.7M × $45 × 12 = $3.1B, plus 1.0M brand × $245 × 12 = $2.9B, ≈ $6.0B/yr federal+state. Eleven states now run Indiana/Arkansas-style adherence-and-weigh-in waivers.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 80+ brands at $6–40/month. Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and China have generic semaglutide, and generic oral semaglutide is available in ~170 countries. Ex-US generic tirzepatide is appearing in China and India ahead of US expiry.
access.note: FICTIONAL. The patent settlement (Jun 2029) allowed licensed generic semaglutide injectable from Jan 2030 (Viatris, Teva, Sandoz, Dr. Reddy's), and Novo launched an authorised generic through a subsidiary. By late 2030 cash prices for generic semaglutide pens and vials are $39–69/month at Cost Plus, Amazon Pharmacy and big-box pharmacies. Generic liraglutide is ~$30–60. Branded orals hold: Wegovy pill and Foundayo starting doses are $149 cash. Lilly cut Zepbound vial cash to $199–299. Retatrutide lists at $1,499 with LillyDirect cash of $499–599 and is no longer allocated after Lilly's Concord and Lebanon capacity came online (Jul 2030). Payer mix of ~48.0M users: commercial 38% (18.2M), Medicare 22% (10.6M), Medicaid 14% (6.7M), cash/direct 24% (11.5M), gray/imported 2% (1.0M) = 100%. Indian mail-order semaglutide has shrunk because domestic generic with a $25 telehealth script costs about the same. The gray market has moved to 'research-peptide' retatrutide and tirzepatide vials sold through gym and supplement channels. Of employers that cover, ~55% require generic semaglutide first and run adherence-gated PBM programmes, and BMI-linked premium surcharges of up to 30% remain legal under federal wellness rules. Access no longer turns on price. It turns on whether a person has a prescriber, a pharmacy, a stable address for weigh-ins and the time to attend them.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, plus US generics and an authorised generic from Jan 2030)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro; brand only in US)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Mar 2028; unallocated from Jul 2030)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Feb 2029, obesity and MASH)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Sep 2029)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking and vaping cessation as adjunct to standard therapy (semaglutide, approved Feb 2029)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction, now routine in EAP and addiction-medicine practice
'metabolic health' / longevity dosing in people without obesity, now split by class: generic microdosing at $39 versus retatrutide-plus-DEXA concierge regimens
self-directed 'drug holidays' and dose-titration around events, travel, pregnancy attempts and creative work
military and police body-composition compliance under formal programmes
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care, still rare
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The triple-agonist driver is realised by retatrutide's supply expansion and the end of allocation (Jul 2030). It is the same 28–30% drug, not a new launch, and best efficacy stays at 28% mean on label. Survodutide was under review and was approved Feb 2029. Amycretin was filed Jun 2028 and approved Sep 2029 after standard review; uptake is modest. MariTide (monthly) is still in phase 3 with readouts in 2030 and no US filing, so it is not on the market. Muscle-preserving adjuncts (bimagrumab combinations) entered phase 3 in 2029 and are not approved. The semaglutide cessation sNDA filed May 2028 was approved Feb 2029. US semaglutide revenue fell ~70% after generic entry. The incretin market is ≈$100B in 2030: US volume nearly doubled, but semaglutide generic erosion offset it.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Most common class effect. Generic self-titration without escalation schedules has raised ER visits for vomiting and dehydration among new cash-pay starters.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; FDA generic-labelling patient guide on titration (2030).

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (mass-tort litigation)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Ileus and obstruction are labelled. Whether gastroparesis persists after stopping is disputed. MDL 3094 (E.D. Pa.) passed ~55,000 filed claims in 2030 after generic entry brought new users and law-firm advertising. Under PLIVA v. Mensing generic makers are largely shielded, so claims target Novo and Lilly, including claims by generic users under 'innovator liability' theories in a few states.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: First bellwether plaintiff verdict (May 2030); class label wording on persistent delayed gastric emptying strengthened; settlement talks ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal confirmation in long-term data; absolute risk low. Joined to MDL claims, and pancreatic-cancer claims are pleaded but scientifically weak.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; litigation now at mass-tort scale.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Rare, but it is now a standard pre-procedure question. Endoscopy and surgery cancellations from retained gastric contents are common at high-uptake hospitals.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; anaesthesia society hold/diet guidance; part of MDL claims.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss; rising in absolute numbers as retatrutide use spreads.
Population problem among users 65+; lean share of loss ~25–40%. Users who do resistance training show markedly less loss, which tracks income.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label update (2028); DEXA and counselling now a condition of Medicare demo coverage.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: HR ~1.3–1.4 for fragility fracture in 65+ long-term users, worst in women and cyclers. New concern about stress fractures in young military trainees who combine the drug with high-load training.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling; DEXA recommended; Senate HELP report (2029) faulted Novo's disclosure; DOJ civil matter unresolved.

safety_ledger.effect: Stress fractures in young adults in high-load training (military, police academy)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Army Public Health Center surveillance flags higher tibial and metatarsal stress-fracture rates in trainees on the drug during initial training; confounded by entry weight.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DoD pauses drug initiation during the first 10 weeks of basic training (2030); study ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare'; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in large datasets, including the cessation trials.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The retatrutide postmarketing anhedonia scale shows a small dose-dependent signal; survey estimates remain ~10–15% of long-term users. Drug holidays are widely used to manage it, which complicates measurement.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA added a 'mood and motivation' patient-information paragraph (2030) without a warning; cessation label cites reduced craving as the mechanism.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Most regain within a year. Holidays of 2–4 weeks produce partial regain and GI re-escalation on restart.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; Indiana waiver litigation continues.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Signals for iron, B12, vitamin D and protein, larger in unmonitored cash-pay users.
About eight years of follow-up exist. Adolescent bone-accrual studies have enrolled but not reported. Pediatric exposure has more than doubled.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; pediatric bone-accrual study ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Indian mail-order harms fell. Poison-centre calls about 'research-use' retatrutide vials from gyms and supplement sites are rising.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts; FDA warning letters to peptide sellers; first criminal referrals (2030).

food_and_beverage.state: Contraction resumed and has reached the value tier: unit volume of snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks fell faster in 2030 than in any year since 2024 as bottom-third uptake doubled. Dollar-store snack aisles shrank. Makers push protein-fortified 'small-format' packs and SNAP-eligible protein drinks. The 'bone-health' claim is ubiquitous.

alcohol.state: Still contracting. The cessation approval turned tobacco into the louder story: cigarette and nicotine-pouch volumes fell sharply as quitlines in 30 states began supplying generic semaglutide with NRT. Spirits volume is down mid-single digits again, and premium 'one good drink' formats are the only growth.

restaurants.state: Fine dining and protein-forward fast casual are stable. Value-volume quick-service and buffets in lower-income markets lost traffic once generics reached their customers, and dollar-menu chains cut portion sizes and prices together.

apparel.state: Size runs shift down in mass retail. 'Fitted strength' cuts showing shoulders and arms are the premium signal. Plus-size specialists contract again as cycling slows.

fitness.state: Two tiers: DEXA-plus-coaching studios and longevity clinics for the top third, and mandated or subsidised strength programmes (Medicare demo counselling, Army and police PT) for everyone else. Budget gyms grow on 'prescribed lifting' referrals.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend fell from ~+9% to ~+3% on generic substitution. Employer coverage rose to 66% because covering generic semaglutide is cheap. Conditionality got tighter rather than looser: generic-first steps, adherence gating, BMI-linked surcharges and weigh-in verification. Carriers face MDL-related subrogation questions.

pharma.state: Lilly dominates on tirzepatide and retatrutide, brands that generics cannot touch before 2031–32. Novo's US semaglutide revenue collapsed after the settlement, and its authorised generic keeps some volume. Generic makers (Viatris, Teva, Sandoz, Dr. Reddy's) are capacity-constrained on pens. The MDL reserve is the overhang for both brand firms.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Lean is no longer a signal, because anyone with $45 can get lean. What reads now is lean and strong versus lean and soft: visible shoulders, a good posture and a DEXA app showing lean-mass percentile mark money and time. Thin arms, a flat seat and 'Medicaid face' mark generic users without coaching. Regain is read as a holiday gone long.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use is 21% in the top third and 14.2% in the bottom third; the gap is narrower, but the bodies differ more. The top third runs retatrutide or tirzepatide with DEXA, protein coaching and trainers. The bottom third runs generic semaglutide at $39–69 with a pharmacy-kiosk scale. Locally, in Fayetteville, North Carolina, around Fort Bragg, enlisted soldiers on the Army's Metabolic Readiness programme and their spouses on cash generics have made weekly pen day a household routine, and the off-post gyms sell 'tape-test prep'. In Austin and Scottsdale the longevity clinics sell muscle the way they once sold thinness.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are smaller everywhere. Holiday 'holidays' are common: people skip a dose before Thanksgiving or a wedding so they can eat, and hosts plan for guests who are re-escalating and nauseous. Workplace potlucks have largely died.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: The 'on/off' filter is mostly obsolete. Profiles now list 'lifts', lean-mass percentile, or which drug a person is on, and 'reta' carries status. Couples negotiate synchronised holidays.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is a dial people expect to control, and leaving it unmanaged reads as either a luxury or a failure depending on income. Smoking has become strongly marked as a class-and-region trait as cessation use spreads.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Surveys put persistent reduced pleasure at ~10–15% of long-term users, higher on retatrutide's top doses. A 2030 consumer poll finds ~40% of users have taken at least one deliberate 'holiday' to 'feel like myself', and about a quarter titrate below label dose for mood rather than tolerance. Cheap generics make self-titration easy, and adherence-gated plans treat it as non-compliance.
interior_life.framing: Called 'the flatness' or 'being on-flat'. It is a familiar complaint, like SSRI blunting in the 2000s, with a vocabulary of holidays, micro-dosing and 'creative dosing'. Clinicians still say 'reward modulation'. Cessation marketing calls the same effect craving relief, and the Army calls it discipline.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Two regimes are colliding. Employers and the military reward continuous adherence: PDC dashboards, weigh-ins and police and Army body-composition rules. Workers want flexibility to holiday, and some unions (SEIU, Teamsters, the Fraternal Order of Police in several cities) have won 'medical holiday' clauses that pause adherence gating for up to 21 days a year. Creative, sales and hospitality workers openly dose low. Shift workers on Amazon and UPS night schedules use the drug to blunt night-shift eating.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Off-dose is an aesthetic. Musicians announce 'holiday records', and 'on-flat' is a critic's insult for affectless pop. Gaming and gambling firms note lower spend per user in high-uptake ZIP codes. Festival season is when drug holidays peak.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Synchronised holidays around anniversaries and conception attempts are common advice. Couples therapists routinely ask about dose. Mismatched desire is a standard complaint in relationship columns, framed as fixable by scheduling.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The fights are over control of the dial. Who decides whether a holiday counts as non-adherence? Must police officers and soldiers stay on? Can benefit gating override a doctor's taper? The Indiana waiver case and an Army Inspector General review keep it in the news. There is speculation about a 'flat electorate', but no measured effect on turnout.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access by default now that prices have collapsed. FDA is defensive on GI and bone safety under the MDL and the Senate HELP report, and is starting criminal enforcement against research-peptide sellers. Generic approvals were fast-tracked after the settlement.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No civilian mandate. The Medicare Metabolic Health Demonstration replaced the Bridge (generic-first, conditioned on adherence and DEXA). Thirty state quitlines supply generic semaglutide for cessation. Medicaid coverage is state-by-state, now mostly generic.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning is the norm: 11 Medicaid waivers on the Indiana/Arkansas model, ~55% of covering employers with adherence-gated PBM programmes, BMI-linked premium surcharges up to 30%, and Medicare demo adherence rules. Pharmacy-kiosk weigh-ins feed payer portals. Data-sharing with direct supervisors is barred by some union contracts and in Illinois and California, but not federally.
state.workforce_or_military: The DoD Metabolic Readiness Directive (Sep 2029) funds generic semaglutide or tirzepatide through TRICARE and military treatment facilities for service members failing body-composition standards, paired with mandatory strength programming; ~110k active-duty members are enrolled. Initiation is paused during basic training after the stress-fracture signal. FAA guidance (2029) allows pilots on stable-dose incretins after an observation period with no in-flight-incapacitation issues. Several large police departments (Houston, Phoenix, Chicago) offer drug-plus-fitness programmes tied to fitness-for-duty standards. DOT sleep-apnea screening still pulls drivers onto tirzepatide.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The India price gap no longer works as a stump line now that US generics are $39–69. The new issues are API dependence (Indian and Chinese peptide API in US generic pens), Section 232 tariffs on finished pens (generics are partly exempted), and DoD pressure for domestic fill-finish as 'readiness infrastructure'.

still_true: Retatrutide's list price remains $1,499 a month.
No generic tirzepatide is sold in the US; Lilly's tirzepatide exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32 or later.
Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still condition Medicaid GLP-1 coverage on ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout after two misses.
Foundayo and the Wegovy pill starting doses are still ~$149–150 a month cash through manufacturer direct channels.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

events.event: FDA approves semaglutide as an adjunct for smoking and vaping cessation; within a year 30 state quitlines add it alongside NRT, and tobacco majors cut volume guidance

Novo Nordisk settles Paragraph IV litigation with Viatris, Teva, Sandoz and Dr. Reddy's, licensing US generic semaglutide entry from January 2030, and announces an authorised generic; by late 2030 pens sell for $39–69 a month cash

Pentagon issues the Metabolic Readiness Directive, funding GLP-1 therapy plus mandatory strength training for service members failing body-composition standards; FAA clears stable-dose incretin use for certificated pilots

CMS lets the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge lapse and replaces it with a generic-first Metabolic Health Demonstration conditioned on refill adherence and annual DEXA; three more states win Indiana-style Medicaid adherence waivers
First bellwether jury in the GLP-1 multidistrict litigation finds Novo Nordisk failed to warn of persistent gastroparesis; filed claims pass 55,000 as generic-era users join
Lilly ends retatrutide allocation as new capacity opens and offers $499 LillyDirect cash pricing; 'reta plus DEXA' packages spread through longevity clinics

open_tensions: Cheap generics made the drug universal, but conditional coverage, military rules and adherence dashboards demand continuous use, while users increasingly take drug holidays to manage the flatness. The fight over who controls the dose is unresolved.
Bone and muscle harms are concentrated among people without coaching or DEXA, so the safety gap now tracks income even as the use gap narrows. Bodies are becoming a cleaner class signal than before.

Mass-tort exposure falls on brand makers while generic makers are shielded by preemption, leaving most new users with no defendant. Settlement, labelling changes or legislation could reset who bears the GI risk.
The Army has made the drug readiness infrastructure just as a stress-fracture signal appears in young trainees, and tirzepatide's 2031–32 generic cliff will reprice the whole system again.

prose.headline: Forty-Five Dollars to Be Thin. Five Hundred to Be Strong. America's New Body Gap.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 nearly one American adult in five is on an incretin drug, close to double the share of two years ago. The change came from price. In June 2029 Novo Nordisk, weakened by a bone-data scandal and a Senate report, settled its patent fights with four generic makers and licensed US generic semaglutide from January 2030. By autumn a month of generic pens costs $39 to $69 at Cost Plus, Amazon Pharmacy or Walmart. A telehealth prescription adds about the price of a pizza. Roughly two million people who had stopped because of cost in 2027 and 2028 came back, and millions of new users joined them, most from the bottom income third, where use has more than doubled.

Cheap drugs did not make coverage unconditional. They made the conditions cheaper to impose. Covering generic semaglutide costs employers so little that two-thirds now cover weight management. More than half of those require the generic first, track refill adherence and verify weight at pharmacy kiosks. Medicare's Bridge lapsed at the end of 2029 and was replaced by a generic-first demonstration that pays about $55 a month, renews only with steady refills and requires an annual bone scan for anyone over sixty-five. Eleven states now run Medicaid on the Indiana model: miss two refills or two weigh-ins and you are locked out for a year.

The drug has also become part of how the state keeps workers fit for duty. In September 2029 the Pentagon funded GLP-1 therapy and mandatory strength training for service members failing body-composition standards, and about 110,000 are enrolled. The FAA cleared pilots on stable doses. Police departments in Houston, Phoenix and Chicago tie their programmes to fitness-for-duty standards. In 2030 the Army stopped starting recruits on the drug during basic training after its surveillance flagged stress fractures in the shins and feet. Officials describe the pause as a pause.

Semaglutide's smoking-cessation approval in February 2029 widened the market further. Thirty state quitlines now hand out generic pens with nicotine patches, and cigarette and pouch makers have cut their forecasts. Spirits volumes keep falling. Snack makers, who had adapted to affluent users, are losing volume again now that dollar-store customers are on the drug.

Thinness no longer marks class. Lean is cheap, so the class signal is muscle. Retatrutide, the triple agonist that produces surgical-scale loss, came off allocation in July with $499 direct cash pricing. Packages pairing it with a bone scan and a trainer fill longevity clinics in Austin and Scottsdale. People on generics often lose muscle with the fat and have no coach to slow it. Around Fort Bragg in Fayetteville, soldiers on the Army programme and spouses paying cash compare tape-test numbers at off-post gyms that advertise tape-test prep.

The drug's quieting effect is now an ordinary complaint, called the flatness. About two in five users say they have skipped doses deliberately to feel like themselves. People skip before weddings, festivals and anniversaries, and couples plan their skipped weeks together. Unions have won holiday clauses that stop adherence systems counting these weeks as lapses. Where no such clause exists, a holiday counts as non-compliance.

The gastrointestinal litigation has reached mass-tort scale, with more than 55,000 claims and a first plaintiff verdict in May against Novo for failing to warn of lasting gastroparesis. Because federal preemption largely shields generic makers, most new users would have no one to sue. Lilly holds the brands generics cannot yet touch, with tirzepatide's exclusivity running to 2031–32.

Most of the country looks healthier than it did. More people are thinner, fewer smoke, and pharmacy costs are flat. In exchange, more of them stay on schedule for their employer, the military, Medicaid or Medicare.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Keisha Monroe wakes at 5:10 because Darnell's alarm is the loud one. He's already in PT shorts and pinching the pen into his thigh, the beige Army-issue box on the dresser. Weigh-in is Thursday.

She skips hers. Her sister Tasha's wedding is Saturday in Raleigh, and Keisha wants to taste the cake. The Walmart generic is forty-five dollars and nobody counts her refills, so this week she can skip.

At the dental office she cleans six mouths. Two patients mention the burping. One says, before she even asks, "I'm on reta, so if the X-ray light bothers my skin, that's why." He has the shoulders. He paid for the shoulders.

At lunch the front-desk girl is eating a protein cup with a teaspoon, slowly, like it's medicine.

At four, Malik texts from school: Coach says I'd make 165 if I started. Can I. She types no, deletes it, and types after the season.

She stops at the CVS kiosk anyway, out of habit, and steps on. The screen reminds her of nothing because no plan is watching her. Mrs. Pruitt from church is on the next platform with a printed slip, the Medicaid one. If she misses it she's locked out a year. Keisha holds the door for her.

At dinner Darnell eats half a chicken thigh and says it's good. She eats a whole one, then a second, and feels it come back, the old wanting, warm and a little embarrassing.

"You're on holiday," he says. It isn't a question.

"Till Sunday."

He nods and reaches over and takes her hand like he's missed her.
